A disappointment compared to the original trilogy. 

The worldbuilding is very lacking in the Andromeda galaxy. I think the concept is great - a new galaxy to explore with new creatures and alien races. Unfortunately, only 2 new races are introduced, one of which is exclusively a villain/enemy race with no redeeming qualities whatsover, leaving only one new race to interact with. Most of the worlds are either barren or populated by settlers from the Milky Way (Salarians, humans, asari, turians and krogan) making it feel nearly indistinguishable from frontier planets in that galaxy. 

The gameplay loop is fun enough, although enemies are very spongy on high difficulties. Exploration is made better by an excellent main vehicle, but the game is structured a little like Dragon Age Inquisition with dull MMO-style fetch questing (though not quite as bad) There's too much space with little interesting to do. 

The plot is fine, if predictable. The characters are a real weakness, sadly, compared to any of Bioware's previous games. Character faces look a bit off -  far worse than in Inquisition, oddly enough. Loyalty missions are overly long quest chains, although some are quite creative. The whole game is too long for what it is - too much filler.

I pretty close to 100%-ed the game as I am a huge mass Effect fan, and there is value here for series fanatics. But go in with very low expectations. It's not a great game.
